lesson_title: The Magnet and the Aeroplane: Two Models That Explain the World's Wealth Map
hook_text: Why does Gauteng produce a third of South Africa's GDP on the smallest patch of land? A magnet explains it.
clip_script: Drop iron filings on a table with a magnet in the middle and watch them slide inward. That is how development works. The magnet is the core — the city where the factories, banks and universities cluster. The edges are the periphery, and every January their buses carry the young and the skilled toward the magnet. Geographers call that drain the backwash, and here is the cruel part: everything the magnet attracts makes it stronger. More workers mean more shops, more taxes, better roads — which attract the next factory. Success feeding success. That is why Gauteng, the smallest province, produces about a third of South Africa's entire GDP, and why the pattern repeats at every zoom level: rich North and supplying South globally, Gauteng and the former homelands nationally, office towers and townships inside one city. Now the second model. Rostow said every economy is an aeroplane: parked in traditional farming, then ground crew laying railways and opening banks, then TAKE-OFF — factories multiplying until growth lifts itself. Britain flew it. South Korea flew it. But some planes were fuelled by siphoning other planes' tanks — that is colonialism — and some are still held at the gate by the magnet. Two models: one explains the map, one explains the timeline. Master both and the world's wealth pattern stops being a mystery.
visual_style: Iron filings animating across a map of South Africa toward a glowing Gauteng; zoom transitions from globe to country to single city; then a runway sequence with an aeroplane labelled with Rostow's five stages lifting off a bar chart.
mood: Revelatory and slightly subversive, ending confident.
pacing: Hypnotic slow pull on the filings, accelerating through the zoom levels, full-speed take-off roll for the Rostow half.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any region's future off the two models.
